subject: Film & Cinema
title: Aspect Ratios: The Shape of Story
description: A 60-second lesson on Aspect Ratios: The Shape of Story.

hook.text: Widescreen epics feel expansive. Boxy 4:3 frames feel intimate. The shape of the frame matters.

buildup.text: CinemaScope's ultra-wide ratio was invented to compete with television in the 1950s.

discovery.text: Some films change aspect ratios mid-story — The Grand Budapest Hotel shifts ratios by era.

twist.text: IMAX uses a nearly square ratio, giving vertical space that standard films cannot match.

climax.text: Aspect ratio isn't technical trivia — it shapes how you perceive every single frame.

punchline.text: The frame's shape is the story's first word.

quiz.question: Why was the CinemaScope widescreen ratio invented?
options: To compete with television by offering a wider visual experience
